He used a quarter of the government's revenue for charity and public welfare.
Agriculture and trade flourished during his time.

He wrote Amuktamalyada in Telugu and Jambavati Kalyana in Sanskrit.

questions.text: Describe the literature of the Vijayanagara period.
questions.text_as_printed: Describe the literature of the Vijayanagara period. (Average)

answer.value:
During the Vijayanagara period, Sanskrit, Kannada, and Telugu literature flourished.
Great poets like Kumaravyasa, Chamarasa, and Ratnakaravarni belonged to this era.
The Vijayanagara period was the golden age of Telugu literature.
Important poets and their works from this period include:
Kumaravyasa - Karnataka Bharatha Kathamanjari
Chamarasa - PrabhulingaLeele
Ratnakaravarni - Bharatesha Vaibhava

questions.text: Explain the causes and consequences of the Battle of Rakkasa Thangadi (Talikota).
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the causes and consequences of the Battle of Rakkasa Thangadi (Talikota). (Difficult)

answer.value:
Causes and Effects of the Battle of Rakkasatangadi (Talikota):
Causes:
The Bahmani kingdom weakened and split into five states.
Taking advantage of this, Rama Raya extended the empire north of the Krishna river, which provoked the battle.
Additionally, the Shahhi Sultans were envious of Vijayanagara's prosperity.
Forgetting their political differences, the Shahhi Sultans united and declared war against Vijayanagara.
Consequences:
Many significant political changes occurred in South India.
The northern part of the empire came under the control of the Bijapur and Golconda states.
Feudatory rulers in Karnataka, such as those of Keladi, Mysore, and Chitradurga, became independent.

During the Vijayanagara period, structures were built using granite stone.

Hazara Rama Swamy Temple
